title: Similarity measurement-based centralized federated learning method

pse.problem: Traditional ML paradigms require large datasets collected by a central server for training models, but in many practical applications of the Internet, data can be sensitive to privacy, and the cost of aggregating large datasets on a central server can be high. This limitation prevents data-driven machine learning from meeting the needs of the IoT systems.
pse.solution_function: The decentralized federated learning method based on similarity measurement solves this problem by training models using decentralized training data in IoT systems without requiring clients to transmit their original datasets, thus reducing communication costs and guaranteeing data privacy.
pse.solution_structure: The solution consists of multiple clients, a server or edge device, and potentially multiple central servers. Clients perform local computations on their own data, and the server or central servers aggregate the results to construct a global model.
pse.solution_implementation: The Federated Average Algorithm (FedAvg) is a key method in this solution. It involves uploading parameters from each client's local model for aggregation and update on the server, allowing the construction of a global model from a subset of clients with non-IID data. Other methods like Fedprox, FedPAQ, and Hyper-Sphere Quantization are also used to further reduce communication costs and improve efficiency.
pse.effect: The result is a decrease in communication costs, preservation of data privacy, and the ability to train models using decentralized training data, making data-driven machine learning suitable for IoT systems.
